subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 24-year-old man presents with a single painful genital ulcer with a yellow-gray exudate and tender, fluctuant inguinal lymph nodes that have begun to drain. He is uncircumcised and reports a new partner 1 week ago. Dark-field microscopy of the ulcer exudate is negative for spirochetes, and PCR for herpes simplex virus is negative.
question: Which organism is most likely responsible for this lesion?
explanation_correct: Haemophilus ducreyi causes chancroid: a painful genital ulcer with exudate and tender inguinal adenopathy that may suppurate. The First Aid mnemonic is that chancroid is so painful you "do cry" (ducreyi). The paired features of a painful ulcer plus tender, draining nodes distinguish it from the painless chancre of syphilis and from the painless ulcer with painful buboes of lymphogranuloma venereum.

explanation_incorrect.A: K granulomatis causes granuloma inguinale, a painless beefy red ulcer that bleeds easily on contact, with Donovan bodies on microscopy.
explanation_incorrect.B: C trachomatis L1-L3 causes lymphogranuloma venereum with painless genital ulcers and painful buboes, so the ulcer itself should not be painful with exudate.
explanation_incorrect.C: N gonorrhoeae causes urethritis and purulent discharge rather than an exudative ulcer with inguinal adenopathy.
explanation_incorrect.D: T pallidum causes a painless chancre with rubbery, nontender regional lymphadenopathy; a painful exudative ulcer with suppurating nodes is not primary syphilis.

educationalObjective: Chancroid from Haemophilus ducreyi is a painful genital ulcer with exudate and tender inguinal adenopathy, in contrast to the painless chancre of syphilis.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 21-year-old woman presents with 2 days of fever, severe pelvic pain, and purulent cervical discharge. She has cervical motion tenderness and adnexal tenderness on bimanual examination. Nucleic acid amplification testing returns positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. The clinician explains that this organism is the most common bacterial sexually transmitted infection in the United States and often presents subacutely, and that treatment must cover both chlamydia and gonorrhea.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for the chlamydial component of this infection?
explanation_correct: Tetracyclines are the agents of choice for chlamydial infection: doxycycline is first line for chlamydial urethritis and cervicitis, and it is also an alternative when a longer course is needed. Tetracyclines accumulate intracellularly and are therefore highly effective against Chlamydia and Rickettsia. PID requires coverage of both pathogens, so ceftriaxone is added for gonorrhea while doxycycline covers C trachomatis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Ceftriaxone is the treatment for gonorrhea, including disseminated infection, but a beta-lactam is not the primary agent for the intracellular chlamydial organism.
explanation_incorrect.C: Metronidazole covers anaerobes and Trichomonas and is not the drug for Chlamydia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Acyclovir treats herpes simplex virus genital infection and has no activity against chlamydia.
explanation_incorrect.E: Benzathine penicillin G is the treatment for syphilis, given to cover T pallidum at each stage.

educationalObjective: Doxycycline is the treatment for chlamydial infection; chlamydia is the most common bacterial STI in the US and requires coverage distinct from gonorrhea.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 31-year-old man presents with multiple painless, beefy red ulcers on the genitals that bleed readily when examined. He is originally from a rural area of a developing country, and the lesions have enlarged slowly over 3 weeks without significant pain. Biopsy shows large macrophages containing bipolar-staining inclusions within the cytoplasm.
question: Which organism is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Granuloma inguinale (donovanosis) is caused by Klebsiella granulomatis, formerly Calymmatobacterium granulomatis, which produces painless, beefy red ulcers that bleed readily on contact. The diagnostic finding is the cytoplasmic Donovan body with bipolar staining seen on microscopy of macrophages. First Aid notes the disease is uncommon in the US.

explanation_incorrect.A: Donovan bodies are intracellular bacteria within macrophages, not fungal structures; there is no fungal agent in the differential for this presentation.
explanation_incorrect.B: H ducreyi produces painful ulcers with exudate and tender nodes, not painless beefy red bleeding ulcers.
explanation_incorrect.C: T pallidum produces a single painless indurated chancre with a clean base and rubbery lymphadenopathy, with spirochetes on dark-field examination rather than Donovan bodies.
explanation_incorrect.E: C trachomatis D-K causes urethritis, cervicitis, and reactive arthritis, while serovars L1-L3 cause lymphogranuloma venereum rather than ulcerative donovanosis.

educationalObjective: Donovanosis (granuloma inguinale) from Klebsiella granulomatis causes painless beefy red ulcers and shows cytoplasmic Donovan bodies.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 27-year-old woman presents with recurrent painful blisters and shallow ulcers on the vulva. She had a similar episode 6 months ago, and each episode is accompanied by bilateral tender inguinal lymphadenopathy and a prodrome of tingling. PCR from a swab of the lesion is positive for herpes simplex virus type 2. Her new partner asks about prevention and about whether the drug eradicates the virus.
question: Which of the following statements best characterizes therapy for this infection?

options.text: Acyclovir resistance arises primarily from mutations in viral DNA polymerase rather than thymidine kinase
Acyclovir is activated by viral thymidine kinase and has no effect on latent virus in sensory ganglia
Acyclovir eradicates latent virus from the sacral dorsal root ganglia, preventing all future recurrences
Acyclovir is activated by cellular kinases only and therefore is equally active against CMV
Foscarnet requires no kinase activation and is the first-line drug for recurrent genital herpes

explanation_correct: Acyclovir is a guanosine analog that is monophosphorylated by HSV/VZV thymidine kinase and therefore is phosphorylated only in infected cells, which limits host toxicity. The triphosphate then preferentially inhibits viral DNA polymerase by chain termination. Because it acts on replicating virus, it has no effect on latent forms of HSV and VZV, so it shortens and suppresses episodes but does not cure infection.

explanation_incorrect.A: Resistance to acyclovir most commonly arises from mutated viral thymidine kinase, which prevents the first phosphorylation step; altered DNA polymerase is the resistance mechanism for foscarnet.
explanation_incorrect.C: Acyclovir has no effect on latent HSV, and latent virus in the sacral ganglia persists, which is why recurrences continue after treatment.
explanation_incorrect.D: Acyclovir is not activated by cellular kinases alone; the requirement for viral thymidine kinase is the basis of its selectivity, and CMV lacks the thymidine kinase needed to activate guanosine analogs, so acyclovir has no activity against CMV.
explanation_incorrect.E: Foscarnet is reserved for acyclovir-resistant HSV and for CMV retinitis when ganciclovir fails; it is not first-line therapy for routine recurrent genital herpes.

educationalObjective: Acyclovir requires viral thymidine kinase for activation, is inactive against CMV and latent HSV, and resistance arises from mutated viral thymidine kinase.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 29-year-old woman presents with a painless ulcer on the cervix incidentally found during a routine pelvic examination. She recalls a painless genital sore 3 weeks earlier that resolved. Rapid plasma reagin is positive, and dark-field microscopy of a lesion exudate shows slender coiled organisms. She is not pregnant and has no drug allergies.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation_correct: This is primary syphilis from Treponema pallidum, and the treatment of choice is benzathine penicillin G given intramuscularly. Penicillin G is the prototype beta-lactam and is active against spirochetes, mainly T pallidum. The painless chancre with regional lymphadenopathy is the defining presentation of primary syphilis in the STI table.

explanation_incorrect.A: Doxycycline is used for chlamydial infection; tetracyclines are an alternative in penicillin-allergic syphilis but are not first-line therapy.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin used for gonorrhea, meningitis, and disseminated Lyme disease; it is not the standard syphilis regimen.
explanation_incorrect.C: Metronidazole treats Trichomonas, bacterial vaginosis, and anaerobes, and it has no role in syphilis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Podophyllin is a topical treatment for condylomata acuminata from HPV, not for a treponemal ulcer.

educationalObjective: Primary syphilis from T pallidum presents as a painless chancre and is treated with intramuscular benzathine penicillin G.
